technique_why: A cozy indoor scene of big simple shapes (a window, a wall, a sill, a blanket and one curled cat) suits painting back to front, with the cat built from an oval and finished in passes.
subject: A gray tabby cat asleep, curled on a yellow knitted blanket on a wooden windowsill, against a blue wall beside a white window with trees outside
focal_point: The cat's sleeping face: the closed eyes, the pink nose and the white muzzle by the paws
light: Daylight comes through the window on the upper left, lighting the left side of the cat, the top of the blanket roll and patches of the sill.
why: We start with the farthest things, the view through the window and the blue wall, then the white frame and the wooden sill, so the room is done before the cat. The blanket goes on next as a flat roll with knit stitches dark then light, and the cat goes on last over everything: a flat gray shape, its shading, the white patches, the stripes, the fur, and the sleeping face at the very end, where the lesson spends most of its steps.

things.name: The sky through the window
things.called: the pale sky outside the window
things.why: A soft pale blue behind the trees, blended in one go.

things.name: The trees through the window
things.called: the green leaves outside the window
things.why: Far leaves dabbed dark then light, soft and without detail since they are outside and far.
things.plain: the dark green dabs of leaves

things.name: The blue wall
things.why: A wall of loose criss-cross blue, deeper and lighter blues blended wet like a sky.

things.name: The white window frame
things.why: A post, a crossbar and the lower ledge built from rectangles, then shaded lavender on the side away from the light.

things.name: The wooden windowsill
things.why: A flat wooden shelf built from two rectangles (the top and the front edge), then shaded and lit with sun patches. Shaped-object has no plank stroke, so the wood is kept to broad pieces.

things.name: The yellow knitted blanket
things.why: A folded roll built from long curved pieces, then knit stitches pressed in dark then light. No element has knit stitches, so the stitches are press-and-lift teardrops in V rows.
things.plain: the plain golden yellow blanket roll
things.left_out: The single strands of yarn: the knit is shown only as rows of teardrop stitches.

things.name: The sleeping tabby cat
things.why: A short-haired cat with stripes and white patches, exactly what this element builds: shape, shade, pale patches, markings, fur, face.
things.left_out: Separate toe pads and single hairs on the paws; the paws are white shapes with a couple of dividing lines.

steps.name: Blend the pale sky in the window

lays.what: the whole left strip of the canvas, the window opening, pale blue at the top fading to near white lower down

steps.after: A pale blue strip runs down the left fifth of the canvas from the top edge to the sill line, painted straight through where the window frame will go. Everything else is bare white canvas.

steps.name: Dab the green leaves outside

lays.what: soft clusters of green leaves filling the lower two thirds of the window strip, with pale sky showing between and above them

steps.after: Soft medium-green leaf clusters fill the lower part of the window strip, with pale sky between them and above. No light leaves yet; the rest of the canvas is bare.

steps.name: Tap the sunny leaves

lays.what: a few yellow-green taps on the tops of the leaf clusters, the side toward the light

steps.after: The leaves outside have yellow-green tops over the darker green. The rest of the canvas right of the window strip is still bare.

steps.name: Criss-cross the blue wall

lays.what: the whole wall right of the window, strong blue with lighter patches worked in, from the top edge down to the sill line, straight through where the cat and blanket will lie

steps.after: Loose criss-crossed blue covers everything right of the window strip from the top edge down to the sill line, running under where the cat and blanket will go. The bottom quarter of the canvas is still bare white.

steps.name: Block in the white frame

lays.what: the white window frame as rectangles: the tall post between the window and the wall, the crossbar across the window, and the deep lower ledge under the window

steps.after: A flat creamy white window frame (a tall post, a crossbar and a lower ledge) sits between the window view and the blue wall, with no shading. The bottom quarter of the canvas is bare.

steps.name: Shade the frame lavender

lays.what: lavender gray strips on the inner face of the post, under the crossbar and along the lower ledge, the sides away from the window light

steps.after: The white frame has soft lavender shadow strips on its inner faces and under the crossbar, so it looks deep. The bottom quarter of the canvas is still bare.

steps.name: Block in the wooden sill

lays.what: the whole windowsill as a flat rust-brown shelf: the top as a wide band and the front edge as a strip along the bottom, painted straight through where the blanket will go

steps.after: The bottom quarter of the canvas is a flat rust-brown sill, running under where the blanket will go, with no shading or sun patches. Wall, frame and window above are done.

steps.name: Darken the sill's front edge

lays.what: deep red-brown along the front edge strip and the right side of the sill top

steps.after: The sill has a dark red-brown front edge and a darker right side. No sun patches yet.
steps.unit: The sill's shadow and sun patches

steps.name: Lay the sun patches on the sill

lays.what: pale peach slanted patches of window light on the left part of the sill top

steps.after: The sill is finished: rust-brown with a dark front edge and peach sun patches on the left. The blanket and cat are not there yet.

steps.name: Block in the blanket roll

lays.what: the whole blanket as flat golden yellow: a long fat roll across the front of the sill built from curved pieces, and the ring rising behind it where the cat will lie, painted straight through under the cat

steps.after: A flat golden yellow blanket roll lies across the sill with its ring rising behind, running under where the cat will lie, with no stitches or shading.

steps.name: Press in the dark stitches

lays.what: deep ochre teardrop stitches in rows of Vs following the curve of the roll, thicker along the bottom of the roll and in the fold between the front roll and the ring

steps.after: The blanket shows rows of dark ochre V stitches following its curves, darkest along the bottom and in the fold, with golden yellow between. No light stitches yet.

steps.name: Press in the light stitches

lays.what: pale yellow teardrop stitches on the tops of the roll and the ring, between the dark ones, on the side toward the light

steps.after: The blanket is finished: a chunky knit roll with dark stitches low and pale yellow stitches on its tops. No cat yet.

steps.name: Block in the curled cat

lays.what: the whole cat as one flat gray shape: a big oval for the curled body, a circle for the head on the left, two triangle ears, and the curved tail and front legs wrapping the front

steps.after: A flat gray cat shape lies curled on the blanket, head on the left with two ears, with no shading, white patches, stripes or face.

steps.name: Shade the cat's far side

lays.what: deep gray curved along the right end of the body, the back, under the tail and under the head

steps.after: The gray cat is darker along its back, right end and underneath, lighter on the left toward the window. Still no white patches, stripes or face.
steps.unit: The cat's shading and white patches

steps.name: Paint the white muzzle, chest and paws

lays.what: creamy white on the muzzle and chin, the patch on the chest behind the head, and the two front paws

steps.after: The cat has a white muzzle, a white chest patch and two white front paws on the gray. No stripes, ear pink or face yet.

steps.name: Pull the dark tabby stripes

lays.what: charcoal stripes curving around the body, the tail and the front leg, and short bars on the forehead

steps.after: The cat has dark tabby stripes wrapping its body, tail, leg and forehead. The ears are still gray inside and there is no face or fur texture.
steps.unit: The cat's stripes, ears and fur

steps.name: Paint the pink inside the ears

lays.what: rosy pink inside both ears

steps.after: Both ears are pink inside. The cat still has no fur texture or face.

steps.name: Flick the light fur

lays.what: short pale silvery-gray flicks over the gray between the stripes, more on the left side toward the light, following the curve of the body

steps.after: Soft pale fur flicks lighten the cat's gray, most on the head and the lit left side, with the stripes and dark showing between. The face is still blank.

steps.name: Line the closed eyes

lays.what: two short downward-curving charcoal lines for the closed eyes, with a tiny lash flick, and a short mouth line under the nose

steps.after: The cat has two curved closed eyes and a small mouth line. No nose or whiskers yet.

steps.name: Press in the pink nose

lays.what: a small pink triangle nose on the white muzzle

steps.after: A small pink nose sits on the white muzzle under the closed eyes. No whiskers yet.

steps.name: Pull the white whiskers

lays.what: thin white whisker lines fanning out from both sides of the muzzle

steps.after: The painting is finished: thin white whiskers fan out from the muzzle of the sleeping tabby on its yellow blanket.
